protocol.suit_handling: all four ordinary suits combined by card number
protocol.hold_definition: a number was kept when at least one card of that number was legal but the model played another number or passed
protocol.memory_test: favorite legal move with normal stored history versus the same decision with earlier history cleared while keeping new public events
protocol.memory_layer_test: on the same turn, erase the earlier memory stage, later memory stage, or all stored history; replay the newest public updates and see whether the favorite legal move or overall choice mix changes
protocol.input_pull_test: on a fixed sample of turns, nudge each of the 94 current-turn numbers slightly and measure how much the favorite's lead over second place moves, adjusted for how much that number usually varies
protocol.memory_map: place sampled 384-value memories on the two display directions that keep the biggest observed differences; the directions have no assigned meaning

findings: Jack - choose the next suit was kept most often: 72.1% of the times it could be played (86,111 chances).
When a rival was down to one or two cards, Joker - next player draws 5 was used +28.6 percentage points more often than when every rival had at least three cards.
Clear all stored history changed the favorite move on 5.7% of otherwise identical card decisions.
Near the sampled decisions, everyone's card counts accounted for 28.9% of what could sway the favorite over the runner-up.
